summary: Mistral released Shieldstral, a 3B-parameter open-weights (Apache 2.0) multimodal safety classifier that evaluates content against plain-language policies specified at inference time, matching or beating guard models up to 7x its size.

mechanisms.reason: A 3B model trained with a specific data-curation and merging technique matches or beats moderation models up to 7x its size while running on a single 16GB GPU, reducing hardware needed per moderation call.
mechanisms.quote: a 3B model that runs on a single 16GB GPU

practices.reason: An open-weights safety classifier that unifies text and image moderation without retraining is directly deployable as a guardrail component in an existing pipeline.
practices.quote: Strong performance — matches or outperforms open guard models up to 7× its size across text safety, refusal detection, policy adaptability, and multimodal benchmarks.

practices.reason: The four-axis benchmark suite (text safety, refusal detection, policy adaptability, multimodal safety) is a candidate methodology to evaluate our own moderation stack, though the eval sets are the lab's own.
practices.quote: We evaluate Shieldstral against open guard models up to 7x its size across four axes. All evaluation samples are held out from training.

practices.reason: Framing moderation as a policy-in-prompt question-answering task with a single yes/no logit readout is a concrete pattern a team could adopt to avoid retraining guardrails per policy change.
practices.quote: you write the policy as a plain-language question at inference time, and the model returns a calibrated safety score. No retraining, one interface for text and images, and a verdict from a single token.
